🌐 Being Safe Online


Welcome to this Learning Experience!
 

In this project, you are going to learn how to be SAFE and RESPONSIBLE on the internet. You will use English to talk about dangers online and what to do to protect yourself and your friends.
 

What are we going to do?
•       Watch videos and read texts about internet safety.

•       Learn key vocabulary in English.

•       Play games and do activities to practise what you learn.

•       Create an interactive INFOGRAPHIC about how to be safe online.

•       Film a short VIDEO showing dangerous situations and how to react.

 

How long?
We will work on this project for 6 sessions (about 45–60 minutes each).

 

What do you need?
•       A device with internet access (tablet, computer, or mobile phone).

•       Your creativity and your English!

 

♿  ACCESSIBILITY NOTE (DUA): All videos have subtitles. All images have descriptions. If you need support in Spanish at any point, ask your teacher.
 

Your final products:


📊 PRODUCT 1

Interactive Infographic

Topic: "How to be safe online"

Tool: Canva or Genially

Must include: clickable elements!

🎬 PRODUCT 2

Short Video (role-play)

Topic: dangerous situations & solutions

Tool: Clipchamp, iMovie or phone

Length: 1–2 minutes

📚 Read and learn: Main dangers online

⚠️ CYBERBULLYING

Cyberbullying means hurting, threatening or making someone feel bad online. It can happen by text, video, photo or social media.

What to do: Don't reply. Block the person. Tell a trusted adult.

🎣 PHISHING

Phishing is when someone pretends to be a real company or person to steal your personal information, like passwords or bank details.

What to do: Don't click suspicious links. Check the email address. Ask an adult.

👤 GROOMING

Grooming is when an adult contacts a child online to gain their trust and then try to harm them. It can happen in games, chats or social media.

What to do: Never meet online contacts in real life. Tell a trusted adult immediately.

⚠️ CYBERBULLYING

Cyberbullying means hurting, threatening or making someone feel bad online. It can happen by text, video, photo or social media.

What to do: Don't reply. Block the person. Tell a trusted adult.

🎣 PHISHING

Phishing is when someone pretends to be a real company or person to steal your personal information, like passwords or bank details.

What to do: Don't click suspicious links. Check the email address. Ask an adult.

👤 GROOMING

Grooming is when an adult contacts a child online to gain their trust and then try to harm them. It can happen in games, chats or social media.

What to do: Never meet online contacts in real life. Tell a trusted adult immediately.

📚 Read: The 10 Golden Rules for Internet Safety

1. Never share your full name, address, phone number or school online.
2. Use a strong password. Mix letters, numbers and symbols. Never share it.
3. Don't talk to strangers online. Only accept contact from people you know in real life.
4. Think before you post. Anything you share online can stay there forever.
5. Don't open suspicious links, files or emails from people you don't know.
6. Tell a trusted adult (parent, teacher) if something online makes you feel uncomfortable or scared.
7. Set screen time limits. Rest your eyes and take breaks every hour.
8. Check if a website is safe (look for 'https://' and the padlock icon).
9. Be kind online. Treat others the way you want to be treated.
10. If someone is unkind to you online: don't reply, block them, and tell an adult.

🎯 Session goals

•       Design an interactive infographic in English.

•       Summarise the main safety tips visually.

•       Practise teamwork and digital creativity.

 

♿  DUA: You can choose the tool you feel most comfortable with: Canva or Genially. You may also work with a partner if you prefer. If English is difficult, write your ideas in Spanish first, then translate them together.

📚 What is an infographic?
An infographic uses images, icons and short texts to explain information in a visual and clear way. Your infographic will be INTERACTIVE — that means it will have clickable elements!

 

📋 Instructions


1.     Open Canva (canva.com) or Genially (genially.com) with your school email.

2.     Choose the template your teacher has shared (see link on Teams).

3.     Add at least 5 internet safety tips in English.

4.     Include at least 3 images or icons.

5.     Add at least 1 interactive element (clickable link, button, animation or tooltip).

6.     Include a title: «How to be safe online».

7.     Write the names of your group members.

8.     When finished: share the link with your teacher on Teams.

💡 Useful language for your infographic

Giving advice Warnings Imperatives

You should...

It's important to...

Make sure you...

Be careful with...

Watch out for...

Never + verb...

Don't share...

Protect your...

Tell an adult...

📤 How to submit it

When your infographic is ready:

1. In Canva: click «Share» > «Copy link». Paste the link in the Teams assignment.

2. In Genially: click «Share» > «Publish» > enable the public link. Copy and paste it.  Your teacher will check that the interactive elements work correctly.

•       At least 3 characters.

•       All dialogue in English (it is OK to speak slowly — clarity is more important than speed!).

•       Duration: 1–2 minutes.
